title: Kyushu-Style Pork Noodle Soup
description: A hearty, warming Kyushu-inspired dish featuring a rich pork broth, springy noodles, and a hint of fermentation. Cozy up with a steaming bowl on a chilly evening.

ingredients.name: Kyushu chili bean paste (Korean chili flakes may be substituted)

instructions: Bring pork bones to a boil in a large pot of water, then reduce heat to a simmer and cook for 30 minutes.
Strain the stock through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot, discarding the solids.
In a separate pan, heat sesame oil over medium heat. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add ground pork and cook until browned, breaking up with a spoon as it cooks.
Stir in chili bean paste, miso paste, and soy sauce. Cook for an additional 1-2 minutes.
Add the fermented chili paste and stir to combine.
Add the cooked noodles to the broth and stir to combine.
Season with honey and sesame seeds to taste.
Divide the noodle mixture among individual bowls and garnish with spring onions, scallions, and additional sesame seeds as desired.
Cook pork to an internal temperature of 63°C / 145°F and let it rest for 3 minutes before serving.
